artifacts.summary: Empirically confirms (via live claude mcp list, ~/.claude.json, and .claude/settings.local.json inspection) that settings.json/settings.local.json mcpServers keys are non-functional for MCP registration; only user-scope ~/.claude.json registers a server. Defines the registration-vs-permission ownership boundary across the four mechanisms, reconciles the lean-lsp wildcard-vs-enumeration duplication, and flags the same dead mcpServers pattern in five other extensions (nix, memory, filetypes, founder, epidemiology).

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system repo, settings.json/settings.local.json's `mcpServers` key (the documented path in extension-system.md for extension-provided MCP servers via settings-fragment.json) is NOT honored by Claude Code (v2.1.227) -- confirmed via `claude mcp list` showing only user-scope ~/.claude.json-registered servers (lean-lsp, playwright) as Connected, while settings.local.json-declared servers (mcp-nixos, obsidian-memory) don't appear at all. Only user-scope ~/.claude.json (via home-manager activation block for static servers, or a core/scripts/ setup script for servers needing per-project computed args) actually registers an MCP server. Six extensions (lean, nix, memory, filetypes, founder, epidemiology) carry this same non-functional mcpServers-in-settings-fragment pattern.

Claude Code subagents inherit MCP tools available in the main conversation (per official docs), but project-scoped .mcp.json servers require an interactive approval prompt that a subagent cannot satisfy -- this approval-prompt deadlock, not a categorical access wall, is the likely real mechanism behind claims like 'subagents cannot access project-scoped MCP servers.' User-scope ~/.claude.json registration has no such approval gate, so it is the reliable choice for servers that subagents must reach.

Wildcard permission grants (mcp__{server}__*) for an MCP server's tools are more maintainable than enumerated tool-name lists: in this repo, lean/settings-fragment.json's 21-tool enumeration for lean-lsp had already drifted out of date (missing lean_minimal_hypotheses and lean_references, both present in the live server), while core's mcp__lean-lsp__* wildcard could not drift by construction. Prefer wildcards for MCP permission grants unless a specific tool must be excluded.
